intro.headline: Ontario Airport’s Search for a Solution
paragraphs: From Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) waivers to multi-vendor agreements, Ontario International Airport Authority’s critical records were fragmented across siloed systems. Finding documents required employees to spend hours manually searching and pulling data.

To address this, OIAA partnered with Madison AI to establish a secure organization-wide record-finding model. Staff adoption surged rapidly in 2026, scaling from 22 initial conversations in July to 344 in September across 67 unique users.

props.title: Isolated Data Workspaces: Tailored Workflows Across Airport Systems
paragraphs: Madison AI organizes OIAA’s workflows into a single platform that handles broad administrative needs, like supporting staff with daily correspondence and drafting. This separation gives employees the speed to manage routine tasks without commingling them with specialized airport systems.

The platform contains two distinct environments: the Agency Management and Governance workspaces, which connect directly to OIAA’s institutional records. It brings together board governance, vendor contracts, financial documentation, and airfield operations into a secure repository. Every response generated can be cited and traced directly back to the source documents, ensuring transparency and auditability.

quote.text: Our team at the Ontario International Airport Authority is remarkably organized, but even with those high standards, finding and accessing institutional knowledge through systems like Laserfiche was a constant hurdle. Madison AI’s organization-wide model successfully solved our knowledge retrieval challenge, making our data more accessible across departments.

props.title: Records scattered across siloed systems
props.intro: Operational efficiency across OIAA’s aviation, commercial, and administrative divisions was hindered by staff spending critical hours manually searching for and assembling files.

items.title: Time-Consuming Research
items.description: Navigating years of vendor agreements, procurement contracts, Construction Manager At Risk provisions, and insurance endorsements required tedious manual searches across disparate systems.

items.title: Scattered Institutional Memory
items.description: Vital context regarding past commission decisions, board delegations, grant authorities, and airport capital budgets was scattered across archives and folders.

items.title: Heavy Administrative Burden
items.description: Experts in airfield safety, finance, and facilities were spending substantial portions of their workweek drafting routine communications, spreadsheet formulas, and staff reports rather than prioritizing high-value operations.

phases.title: Discovering Operational Friction
phases.description: OIAA leadership identified constraints across primary departments, targeting contract review, public relations, and board agenda preparation.

phases.title: Organization-wide Model
phases.description: In collaboration with Madison AI, OIAA rolled out a dual-domain platform for general queries as well as airport operations and governance.

phases.title: Data Integrity and Security
phases.description: The platform was locked within a secure environment, ensuring that OIAA’s internal documents and governance records remain strictly private, protected from commercial model training and verified through source citations.

phases.title: Department-Wide Adoption
phases.description: OIAA experienced rapid user adoption across marketing, finance, contracts, airfield operations and commission governance within 90 days.

phases.title: Expanding to Complex Workflows
phases.description: Staff quickly advanced from simple searches to complex, multi-step workflows.

impact.title: Saving 382 Staff Hours
paragraphs: The partnership between OIAA and Madison AI transformed how airport staff access institutional knowledge and manage daily workflows. By recovering 382 hours of staff time, worth an estimated $38,200, Madison AI and OIAA demonstrated how targeted AI tools can deliver immediate operational ROI in the aviation industry.

By stripping away hours of administrative duties and tedious drafting, OIAA staff can redirect their energy toward expanding air service, optimizing airfield facilities, and fostering regional economic growth.

The success at OIAA serves as a blueprint for aviation authorities and public-sector agencies nationwide. Through collaborative technology, agencies can safely embrace artificial intelligence to safeguard institutional memory and build operational resilience.
